intro.author: Traditionally Daniel, a Judean taken to Babylon as a youth; many modern scholars think the book was completed by a later author
intro.written: Traditionally the 500s BC; many scholars date its final form to about 165 BC, during the persecution under Antiochus IV
intro.audience: Jews living under foreign empires and facing pressure to give up their faith
intro.setting: The book follows Daniel and his friends from Babylon's capture of Jerusalem (605 BC) into the Persian era under Cyrus. Unusually, it is written in two languages: Hebrew (1:1–2:4 and chapters 8–12) and Aramaic, the international language of the day (2:4–7:28).
intro.purpose: To show that God rules over the kingdoms of the world, to encourage faithfulness under pressure, and to assure God's people that his kingdom will outlast every empire.
intro.bigIdea: 'The most High ruleth in the kingdom of men' (4:17), and his kingdom will never be destroyed.
